g.text: Ethernet CBS (IEEE 802.1Qav Credit-Based Shaper) Example Project
RMAC's receive filter defaults to non-promiscuous and
is not touched by Open(). Without this write, externally
received frames addressed to the synthetic test MACs
wait for ETH0 + ETH1 link UP (5 s timeout)
console: "[CBS] ETH0 link: UP ETH1 link: UP"
First Mode Selection (the only blocking prompt)
[1]-[3] port-to-port : disabled / Q0 only / Q1 only
[4]-[6] CPU-generated: disabled / Q0 only / Q1 only
Mode Loop (repeats on every mode change -- no stop step)
build the row table for the selected mode
table and zero the OTHER queue's MAC, so only one
queue is classified and shaped at a time.
steered from the mode's source port:
CBS enabled : Q0 = 10 %, Q1 = 30 % of the link speed
Queues being switched off are committed explicitly
(the driver commits only the queues it enables).
Port0 is the CBS-shaped egress port in every mode.
"MAC table entries: N", "CBS active in hardware (queue mask)"
One fixed frame/descriptor is built once. The queue
index is written into the descriptor's own ipv field --
it is NOT inferred from the destination MAC.
[every cycle, until a different mode number is typed]
SetDescriptor() until the ring is full
one StartDescriptorQueue() for the whole batch
Batched submission lets GWCA auto-chain through
the queued descriptors. 4 slots gives a smooth,
near-continuous stream to the credit shaper.
Needs several hundred Mbps of offered load to
prove a cap -- use a source that delivers >400-500 Mbps.
[every 1 ms, until a different mode number is typed]
-> Wireshark I/O Graph: Q0 ~100 Mbps, Q1 ~300 Mbps
console: "[CBS] WARNING: ETH0 link: .. ETH1 link: .. -- frames cannot flow on a down link"
[a different valid mode number typed (non-blocking check)]
adopt it, go back to the top of the loop
console: "[CBS] Mode N is already active."
